answer: Because the prism stake is held until the velvet settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the vine audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 26% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 56 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. That is 27 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
